study.title: The regulations on cortical activation and functional connectivity of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex-primary somatosensory cortex elicited by acupuncture with reinforcing-reducing manipulation
study.study_design: Randomized crossover within-subject design; 35 healthy participants received ERR, LTRei, and LTRed in a randomized order, each separated by a 1 day washout
study.randomization: The order of performing acupuncture manipulations was generated by a randomization digital table
study.population: Healthy participants recruited from the Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (CDUTCM)
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) right-handed male between the ages of 18 and 40, and (2) with a college degree or higher, and (3) having none of the organic or functional diseases in each system or mental disorders, and (4) having not taken part in any other clinical research in the last 3 months, and (5) given informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) having severe skin disorders, infections, or damaged skin at acupoints, or (2) having a severe needle phobia (headache, dizziness, cold sweat, chest tightness, etc.) or (3) having a score of 50 or above on the Self-rating Depression Scale (SDS) or Self-rating Anxiety Scale (SAS)

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: NIRx Medical Technologies, NY, USA (continuous wave (CW) instrument)
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: continuous wave (CW) fNIRS; two wavelengths of near-infrared light (785 and 830 nm)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 7 min 15 s (5 min resting-state + needle insertion + 1 min 30 s acupuncture manipulation)
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Homer2 toolbox based on MATLAB (R2013b, MathWorks, Inc., Natick, MA, USA)
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: 36-channel Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) coordinates transformed from spatial coordinates of midpoint between each pair of sources and detectors by NIRS-SPM toolbox
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: The channels with too many motion artifacts were rejected by the function hmrMotionArtifactByChannel
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: functional connectivity (FC) using Pearson's correlation coefficients converted to Fisher z-values
statistical_thresholds_exact: FDR p < 0.05 for multiple comparisons for brain regions
p < 0.05 two-tailed for all significance tests
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: false discovered rates method (FDR, p < 0.05); Bonferroni corrections for post-hoc tests
neuroimaging_methods.additional_notes: 16 sources and 13 detectors; 36 channels total; optodes placed on bilateral prefrontal cortex (PFC) and bilateral somatosensory cortex; source-detector distance approximately 3 cm; data collected at 3.096 Hz; preprocessing steps: (1) intensity to OD via hmrintensity2OD; (2) motion artifact rejection via hmrMotionArtifactByChannel; (3) motion correction via hmrMotionCorrectSpline; (4) bandpass filter 0.01-0.1 Hz; (5) OD to hemoglobin via hmrOD2Conc; HbO selected for analysis as most sensitive index

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Table 1 contains MNI coordinates for all 36 channels and their corresponding anatomical locations. This table was not provided in the PDF and exact coordinate values for individual channels could not be extracted. Results are reported at the region/channel label level only.

Supplementary Table 2 contains detailed within-group cortical activation results (presumably t-values, p-values, and channel-level statistics) for ERR, LTRei, and LTRed vs. baseline. This was not provided in the PDF. Activation results were extracted from text descriptions only.

Figure 4 shows cortical activation maps for ERR (A), LTRed (B), and LTRei (C) with channel numbers marked in white (decreased) or black (increased). Detailed statistics for individual channels in within-group contrasts are not reported in text and appear only in Supplementary Table 2.
Figure 3 shows a bar graph comparing needling sensation (C-MMASS) among ERR, LTRei, and LTRed. Individual subscale scores are not reported in the text; only the overall F-statistic is given.

Figure 5B shows post-hoc β-value comparisons for CH21, CH30, and CH36. The exact β-values for each condition are depicted in a figure but not reported numerically in the text (only p-values for comparisons are reported).
Figures 6 and 7 show FC network diagrams. While edge-level statistics are reported in text, channel-to-region anatomical mapping beyond what is stated in text depends on Supplementary Table 1.

The paper reports F(2,28) for CH36 and CH30 between-group comparisons, while F(2,58) is reported for CH21. The different degrees of freedom may reflect missing data for some participants on those channels. This inconsistency is preserved as reported.

Blinding procedures are not described. It is a crossover design with the same practitioner performing all three manipulations; no sham control or blinding of participants or acupuncturist is reported.
Expectancy, credibility, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported. The paper does not mention these measures.
No sham acupuncture or placebo control was included. This is a three-arm active manipulation comparison study only.

The paper states 'all reinforcing-reducing manipulations showed increased FC' compared to baseline (section 3.5) as a general statement, but only LTRei and LTRed showed statistically significant FC increases in specific edges. ERR showed no statistically significant FC differences. The general statement may refer to a trend or refer to the direction of change without significance.

The paper labels CH21 as associated with 'bilateral DLPFC' in the F-statistic reporting but the channel itself is described as right DLPFC in the FC results. This may reflect that CH21 is a right-hemisphere channel used as proxy for bilateral DLPFC effects in the ANOVA. Labels are preserved as reported.

The neuroimaging modality is fNIRS (functional near-infrared spectroscopy), not fMRI. The modality field is set to 'other' since the schema does not have a dedicated fNIRS option; this is noted for downstream meta-analysis coding.
The paper does not report needle retention time separately from the manipulation duration. The manipulation lasted 1 min 30 s; whether the needle remained in place after manipulation is not stated.

The arm-level n_analyzed values of 31 are inferred from the statement 'the remaining 31-participant data were analyzed' and the crossover design (all participants received all three conditions). This is consistent with the F-statistics using repeated measures across all 31 participants.
